note: Single source for the launch checklist. The live page (claude.ai artifact) and release/README.md both read it. Status lives in the live page's database; release/status.json is Claude's copy for the README.

phases.name: Project home
phases.goal: Everything for the game in one place, and a link anyone can play.

steps.title: Project folder on your Artifacts screen
steps.why: One place for the game, this checklist and the bug reports.
how: Folder MONKEY SEE, MONKEY DO on claude.ai > Artifacts.
The playable game, this checklist and the Bug & Feedback page live inside it.
steps.tip: Keep new pages for this game in the same folder so nothing gets lost.
steps.done_when: The folder exists and holds the game.

steps.title: Playable game link (Claude page)
steps.why: A private link you can open on any device right now.
how: Open the 'Monkey See, Monkey Do' page in the folder.
Add #store-test to the end of its link to try the Shop with pretend purchases.
steps.tip: This one is private to you. Testers use the public beta link below.

steps.title: Public beta website built
steps.why: Testers need a normal web link: no account, works on every phone and computer, plays offline, can be added to the home screen.
how: Every web build makes the beta website in dist/site: the game in play/, with a landing page (Play button, QR code, tester notes) in front of it.
Privacy and support pages come with it.
steps.tip: Nothing to do here: it updates itself whenever the game is rebuilt.
steps.done_when: dist/site holds the landing page and the game, tested offline.

steps.title: Put the beta website on GitHub Pages
steps.why: A free public web address that works on every phone and computer.
how: GitHub Pages was already on for this repository: it serves the gh-pages branch, home of the Off-Grid Survival Kit.
The game gets its own monkey-see-monkey-do/ folder there. bash scripts/deploy_beta.sh publishes it and never touches the Off-Grid files.
steps.tip: Nothing to switch on. (GitHub's Pages settings page shows a 404 unless you are signed in as the repository owner.)

steps.title: Claude checks the live beta link
steps.why: So you never send testers a broken link.
how: Claude opens the link as an iPhone, an Android phone and a desktop browser.
Checks the game starts, a level plays and it reopens offline.
steps.tip: Claude re-checks the link after each new beta build.

phases.name: Beta test
phases.goal: Real people on real phones find the small bugs before any store reviewer does.

steps.title: Recruit 12 or more testers
steps.why: Google Play makes new personal accounts run a closed test with at least 12 testers for 14 days in a row. Recruit them now and use the same group for both.
how: Aim for a mix: iPhone, Android (including an older one), a tablet, a computer.
Include at least two kids in the target age, with a parent present.
Write down each tester's Google account email (needed for the Play closed test later).
steps.tip: Ask 15-16 people: some always drop out, and Google counts only testers who stay opted in for all 14 days.
steps.done_when: 12+ people said yes and you have their emails.

steps.title: Send testers the beta link
steps.why: One link works on every device, no install.
how: Send https://namastegeitz.github.io/Eddie-G/monkey-see-monkey-do/ (or the QR code in release/01-web-beta/qr.png).
Ask them to play for 15 minutes on two different days.
steps.tip: Give them three concrete asks: finish levels 1-5, play with a game controller or keyboard if they have one, open the Wardrobe.

steps.title: Invite testers to the Bug & Feedback page
steps.why: Reports land in one place, with the device details filled in, and Claude can read them and fix bugs.
how: Open 'Monkey Do Bug & Feedback' in the project folder.
Share > invite each tester by email as Editor (the only level that lets people outside an organization write).
Testers can only add to their own reports; only you change a report's status.
steps.tip: If a tester has no Claude account, ask them to text you instead and type their report in yourself: it takes 30 seconds.

steps.title: Real-device pass: iPhone, Android, tablet, computer
steps.why: Touch feel, sound timing and speed can only be judged on real hardware.
how: On each device: play levels 1-3, a beach and a moon level, Endless for 5 rounds.
Try Add to Home Screen, then play with Wi-Fi off.
Note anything that feels slow, laggy or confusing as a report.
steps.tip: On older phones, check Settings > Graphics: Auto should drop to Medium or Low by itself within a few seconds.
steps.done_when: Each of the four device types played a full session.

steps.title: Fix the minor bugs from reports
steps.why: Small fixes now avoid one-star reviews later.
how: Claude reads the Bug & Feedback page, reproduces each bug, fixes it, runs all tests, and marks it Fixed with a note.
steps.tip: Ask Claude 'check the bug reports' any time; it reads them directly.
steps.done_when: No open Minor or Major reports older than a week.

steps.title: Beta sign-off
steps.why: A clear go/no-go before paying any store fees.
how: No open Crash or Major reports.
Average fun rating 4 or higher.
You'd be happy for a stranger to download it today.
steps.tip: If the fun rating is low, read the 'Confusing' reports first: they usually point at one unclear screen.

phases.name: Store kit (used by every store)
phases.goal: Write it once, paste it everywhere: icons, screenshots, text, policies, ratings.

steps.title: Check the name is free to use
steps.why: A name clash can get the app pulled after launch.
how: Search 'Monkey See Monkey Do' on the App Store, Google Play, Steam and itch.io.
Search the US trademark database (tmsearch.uspto.gov) for game titles.
If crowded, keep 'Monkey See, Monkey Do' as the title and use 'Monkey Do' as the short name (already the home-screen name).
steps.tip: Store titles can add a short tag that also helps search, e.g. 'Monkey See, Monkey Do: Dance' (30 characters max on both mobile stores).

steps.title: Public privacy policy page
steps.why: Apple, Google, Steam and Microsoft all ask for a privacy policy link.
how: Published with the beta site (from PRIVACY.md).
steps.tip: Live: https://namastegeitz.github.io/Eddie-G/monkey-see-monkey-do/privacy.html

steps.title: Support page and contact
steps.why: Apple requires a support URL; every store shows a contact.
how: Claude built /support.html (FAQ + how to report a problem).
You choose a contact email to show on it (a new address just for the game is a good idea).
steps.tip: Use a dedicated address, e.g. monkeydo.support@gmail.com, so store mail doesn't flood your personal inbox.
steps.done_when: The support page shows your chosen contact.

steps.title: Store icons (1024 and 512 px)
steps.why: Apple needs 1024x1024 without transparency; Google Play needs 512x512.
how: Generated into release/00-shared/icons from the game's icon.
steps.tip: Don't add words or a border: stores round the corners themselves.
steps.done_when: Both PNGs exist at exact sizes.

steps.title: Phone screenshots at store sizes
steps.why: Apple needs 6.9-inch iPhone (1320x2868); Google Play needs 2-8 phone shots.
how: Rendered from the real game into release/00-shared/screenshots (title, watch, your turn, moon, disco, wardrobe).
steps.tip: The first two screenshots sell the game: they show the dancing monkey and the copy buttons.

steps.title: Tablet screenshots
steps.why: The iPad app needs 13-inch iPad shots (2064x2752); Play shows tablet shots on tablets.
how: Rendered into release/00-shared/screenshots/ipad-13.
steps.tip: If you ever turn off iPad support, Apple stops asking for these.

steps.title: Desktop screenshots (1920x1080)
steps.why: Steam, GOG, itch.io, Microsoft and Epic use landscape shots.
how: Rendered into release/00-shared/screenshots/desktop-1080p.
steps.tip: Steam wants at least 5; show different maps so the page looks varied.

steps.title: Store text: names, descriptions, keywords
steps.why: Each store has its own limits; drafts that fit are ready to paste.
how: Claude drafted release/00-shared/store-text.md with every field at the right length.
You read it and change anything that doesn't sound like you.
steps.tip: Lead with what you do in the first 5 seconds: 'Watch the monkey dance. Copy the moves.'

steps.title: Google Play feature graphic and itch.io cover
steps.why: Play requires a 1024x500 feature graphic; itch.io uses a 630x500 cover.
how: Rendered into release/00-shared/art.
steps.tip: Keep important parts away from the edges: Play crops it on some screens.
steps.done_when: Both images exist at exact sizes.

steps.title: Age-rating answers
steps.why: Every store asks the same kinds of questions (violence, purchases, chat...).
how: Claude prepared release/00-shared/age-rating.md with honest answers for IARC (Google, Microsoft, Epic), Apple's questionnaire and Steam's content survey.
You submit them in each store.
steps.tip: Answer 'yes' to in-app purchases on mobile. Expect 4+ / Everyone everywhere.
steps.done_when: You submitted ratings in each store you launch on.

steps.title: Decide price per store
steps.why: Mobile and PC players expect different models.
how: Suggested: free with optional packs on iPhone and Android (already built).
PC stores (Steam, GOG, itch.io desktop): a one-time price ($4.99 suggested) and no in-game Shop. Steam requires its own payment system for in-game purchases.
itch.io web: free or pay-what-you-want.
steps.tip: A small PC price with no extra purchases suits GOG best: it's the type of game it curates.
steps.done_when: You wrote down the price for each store.

steps.title: Short trailer (optional)
steps.why: Steam and GOG pages convert much better with a 30-60 second video.
how: Record the screen while playing: title, a watch round, a copy round with Perfect sparkles, three maps, the wardrobe.
Claude can script the shots and add captions.
steps.tip: Show gameplay in the first 3 seconds; no logos first.
steps.done_when: An MP4 at 1920x1080 is in release/00-shared/art.

phases.name: Google Play (Android)
phases.goal: Free app with optional packs, live on Google Play.

steps.title: Meets Google's current Android requirement (API 36)
steps.why: Since 31 Aug 2026, new apps and updates must target Android 16 (API level 36).
how: The Android project targets and compiles with API 36; minimum is Android 7.0 (API 24).
steps.tip: Each August Google raises this again; Claude can bump it with one change.

steps.title: Create a Google Play Console account
steps.why: Needed to publish anything on Google Play.
how: play.google.com/console > sign up ($25 one-time).
Personal account: ID verification, then the 12-tester rule applies.
Organization account: needs a D-U-N-S number, skips the 12-tester rule.
steps.tip: Personal is fine for one person; the 14-day test is your beta group anyway.

steps.title: Get a machine that can build Android
steps.why: This cloud project can't download Google's Android tools (dl.google.com is not allowed here).
how: Easiest: install Android Studio on your computer and open mobile/android.
Or: allow dl.google.com in this project's environment and Claude builds it here.
steps.tip: Allowing dl.google.com lets Claude build and test the APK and AAB itself, with no setup on your side.

steps.title: Create the upload key and back it up
steps.why: Google needs every update signed with the same key. Lose it and you need Google support to reset it.
how: keytool command is in release/03-google-play/README.md.
Save the .jks file and both passwords in a password manager and one offline place.
steps.tip: Use Play App Signing (the default): Google keeps the real signing key, you keep only the upload key.

steps.title: Build the signed release bundle (.aab)
steps.why: Google Play only accepts Android App Bundles.
how: cd apps/monkey-see-monkey-do && node scripts/build_web.mjs && cd mobile && npx cap sync android
Android Studio: Build > Generate Signed App Bundle, or ./gradlew bundleRelease with keystore.properties.
Copy the .aab into release/03-google-play/build/.
steps.tip: Bump versionCode by 1 for every upload, even test ones.

steps.title: Create the app in Play Console
steps.why: Holds the listing, tests and releases.
how: Create app > name, default language English (US), Game, Free.
Package name comes from the first upload: com.namastegeitz.monkeydo.
steps.tip: Choose 'Free': a free app can never be changed to paid on Google Play (packs are still allowed).
steps.done_when: The app appears in your Play Console list.

steps.title: Fill in the store listing
steps.why: What players see before they install.
how: Paste from release/00-shared/store-text.md (title 30, short 80, full 4000 characters).
Icon 512x512, feature graphic 1024x500, 2-8 phone screenshots, tablet screenshots.
Category: Music or Puzzle. Contact email. Privacy policy URL.
steps.tip: Play shows the first 3 screenshots in search: put the dancing monkey first.

steps.title: App content: data safety, ads, rating, audience
steps.why: Google won't release an app until every App content section is done.
how: Data safety: no data collected or shared (answers in release/03-google-play/data-safety.md).
Ads: no ads.
Content rating: IARC questionnaire (answers in release/00-shared/age-rating.md).
Target audience: if you include under-13s, the Families policy applies: parental gate before purchases is already built.
steps.tip: Choosing age groups under 13 adds a review step but opens the 'Kids' area of Play. The game already meets the rules (no ads, no data, grown-up check).
steps.done_when: App content page shows all green.

steps.title: Payments profile and 26 in-app products
steps.why: The Shop's packs, bundles and sets must exist in Play with the exact IDs.
how: Set up a payments profile (Settings > Payments profile).
Upload a build with billing first (internal testing), then Monetize > Products > In-app products.
Create each product from docs/STORE_PRODUCTS.md with the same ID and price.
steps.tip: Add yourself as a license tester (Settings > License testing) so test purchases never charge.

steps.title: Closed test: 12 testers for 14 days
steps.why: Required for new personal accounts before production access.
how: Testing > Closed testing > create track, upload the .aab.
Add your testers' Google emails, share the opt-in link.
Keep at least 12 opted in for 14 days straight; Claude fixes what they find.
steps.tip: The 14 days only count while 12 or more are opted in, so start with extra testers.

steps.title: Apply for production and release
steps.why: The final step to go live.
how: Dashboard > Apply for production (answer the questions about your test).
Create a production release, roll out to 100% (or 20% first to be careful).
steps.tip: First reviews usually take 1-7 days. Answer every review with the fix version number.
steps.done_when: The game is on Google Play.

phases.name: Apple App Store (iPhone and iPad)
phases.goal: Free app with optional packs, live on the App Store.

steps.title: Join the Apple Developer Program
steps.why: Required to publish on the App Store (and to sign Mac builds).
how: developer.apple.com/programs/enroll, $99/year.
Individual: your legal name shows as the seller. Organization: needs a D-U-N-S number.
steps.tip: Enroll from the Apple Developer app on an iPhone: ID verification is often faster there.
steps.done_when: You can sign in to App Store Connect.

steps.title: A Mac with Xcode 26, or Codemagic
steps.why: Apple builds need Xcode 26 and the iOS 26 SDK (required since April 2026), which only run on macOS.
how: Your own Mac: install Xcode from the App Store, open mobile/ios/App/App.xcodeproj.
No Mac: Codemagic's cloud Macs (config ready in mobile/ci/codemagic.yaml, free tier for small apps).
steps.tip: Codemagic can upload straight to TestFlight once you add an App Store Connect API key.
steps.done_when: An iOS build runs on a Mac or Codemagic.

steps.title: Paid Apps agreement, tax and banking
steps.why: In-app purchases don't work until this is complete, even for free apps.
how: App Store Connect > Business: accept Paid Apps, add bank account and tax forms.
steps.tip: Do this early: approval can take a few days.

steps.title: Create the app in App Store Connect
steps.why: Holds the build, listing and purchases.
how: Register bundle ID com.namastegeitz.monkeydo (Identifiers).
My Apps > + > New App: iOS, name, English (US), the bundle ID, SKU monkeydo-001.
steps.tip: The name must be unique on the App Store; have a backup ready from the name check.
steps.done_when: The app appears in My Apps.

steps.title: Create the 26 in-app purchases
steps.why: The Shop needs each product to exist with the exact ID.
how: Monetization > In-App Purchases: create each from docs/STORE_PRODUCTS.md (type, ID, name, description, price).
Add a review screenshot of the Shop (release/00-shared/screenshots/shop-review/01-shop.jpg).
steps.tip: Try every purchase first in the iPhone Simulator with MonkeyDo.storekit: no account needed.

steps.title: Build and upload with Xcode 26
steps.why: The binary Apple reviews.
how: node scripts/build_web.mjs && cd mobile && npx cap sync ios
Xcode: set your Team, add the In-App Purchase capability, Product > Archive > Distribute > App Store Connect.
steps.tip: Bump the build number for each upload; the version stays 1.0.0 until release.
steps.done_when: The build shows in App Store Connect > TestFlight.

steps.title: TestFlight beta
steps.why: Real iPhones with real (sandbox) purchases before review.
how: Add yourself as an internal tester; invite beta testers by email for external testing (short Apple review first).
steps.tip: External testing reuses the same testers as the web beta: just send them the TestFlight link.
steps.done_when: At least 3 people played the TestFlight build.

steps.title: App Privacy: Data Not Collected
steps.why: Shown on the App Store page; must match what the app does.
how: App Privacy > Get Started > 'No, we do not collect data from this app'.
steps.tip: True for this game: purchases are handled by Apple, and the save stays on the phone.

steps.title: Age rating questionnaire
steps.why: Apple's 2025 ratings (4+, 9+, 13+, 16+, 18+) need the updated questions answered.
how: Use the Apple section of release/00-shared/age-rating.md. Expected result: 4+.
steps.tip: 'In-app purchases: yes' doesn't raise the rating.

steps.title: Decide: Kids Category or not
steps.why: The Kids Category puts the game in front of parents but adds strict rules.
how: Kids Category needs: no third-party ads or analytics (none here) and a parental gate before purchases and outside links (already built: the grown-up check).
steps.tip: Suggested: not Kids Category at first (simpler review); age rating 4+ already makes it family-friendly.

steps.title: App Store listing
steps.why: What people see in the App Store.
how: Paste from release/00-shared/store-text.md: name 30, subtitle 30, promotional text 170, description 4000, keywords 100 (commas, no spaces).
Screenshots: 6.9-inch iPhone (1320x2868) and 13-inch iPad (2064x2752).
Support URL and privacy policy URL from the beta site.
steps.tip: Keywords: don't repeat words already in the name or subtitle; Apple indexes those already.

steps.title: Submit for App Review
steps.why: Apple checks every app before release.
how: Add the build to version 1.0, attach the in-app purchases, write review notes (draft in release/04-apple-app-store/review-notes.md), submit.
steps.tip: Most reviews finish in 1-2 days. If rejected, Claude can fix and you resubmit the same day.

phases.name: itch.io (web and PC, fastest store)
phases.goal: Playable in the browser on itch.io this week, free or pay-what-you-want.

steps.title: HTML5 upload zip
steps.why: itch.io plays a zip with index.html at its root right in the page.
how: release/02-itch-io/monkey-see-monkey-do-html5.zip (rebuilt by scripts/build_release.mjs).
steps.tip: Well under itch.io's limits (500 MB unpacked, 200 MB per file).
steps.done_when: The zip exists and plays when unzipped.

steps.title: itch.io account and payouts
steps.why: Free to join; payouts only matter if you charge.
how: itch.io > Register > 'I'm interested in distributing content on itch.io'.
Payment settings: PayPal or Stripe if you want tips.
steps.tip: Pay-what-you-want with $0 minimum gets the most players and still allows tips.

steps.title: Create the project page
steps.why: Where people play.
how: Dashboard > Create new project: kind HTML.
Upload the zip, tick 'This file will be played in the browser'.
Embed: 'Click to launch in fullscreen' and 'Mobile friendly' (portrait).
Paste the itch.io text from store-text.md; cover 630x500; screenshots.
steps.tip: Fullscreen launch avoids a small embedded box on phones.
steps.done_when: The page plays the game in draft.

steps.title: Publish on itch.io
steps.why: Your first public store release.
how: Visibility: Public. Add tags: rhythm, memory, music, casual, family, dance.
steps.tip: Post the link in the itch.io 'Release Announcements' forum and add it to a few jams' showcases.

phases.name: PC edition (Windows, Mac, Linux)
phases.goal: A desktop app for Steam, GOG, Microsoft Store and Epic: one-time price, no in-game Shop.

steps.title: Desktop app project (Electron)
steps.why: PC stores need an installed app, not a web page.
how: release/05-desktop: Electron app that opens the game full screen, offline, with its own window and icon.
steps.tip: Electron runs on Windows, macOS and Linux from one project.

steps.title: PC edition: hide the real-money Shop
steps.why: Steam requires in-game purchases to go through Steam; a one-time price with no Shop is simpler and suits GOG.
how: The desktop app runs the game with ?edition=pc: no Shop button and no 'buy in the apps' text; everything is earned by playing.
steps.tip: Skins and gear stay earnable with bananas and golden bananas, so nothing is lost.

steps.title: Build Windows, macOS and Linux apps
steps.why: The files you upload to Steam, GOG and the others.
how: On a computer with Node.js: cd apps/monkey-see-monkey-do/release/05-desktop && npm install && npm run build:win (or :mac / :linux).
Or allow github.com downloads here and Claude builds the Linux and Windows versions.
steps.tip: Build on Windows for the Windows app and on a Mac for the Mac app; signing works best on its own system.

steps.title: Code signing (Mac required, Windows recommended)
steps.why: Unsigned Mac apps won't open; unsigned Windows apps show a warning (Steam and GOG installs avoid most of it).
how: Mac: Developer ID certificate + notarization (uses the $99 Apple account).
Windows: optional code-signing certificate; Microsoft Store signs for you.
steps.tip: For Steam-only Windows release you can skip a Windows certificate at first.

steps.title: Test the PC builds
steps.why: Keyboard play, window resizing and offline start need a real PC check.
how: Play with the keyboard (Q W E / A S D), resize the window, go full screen (F11), start with Wi-Fi off.
steps.tip: Also try a laptop with only integrated graphics: Auto graphics should keep it smooth.
steps.done_when: Played 15 minutes on Windows (and Mac if you sell there).

phases.name: Steam
phases.goal: A Steam store page collecting wishlists, then release.

steps.title: Steamworks partner account
steps.why: Steam's developer side.
how: partner.steamgames.com > join; identity, tax and bank details.
steps.tip: Takes a few days to verify: start before the build is finished.
steps.done_when: You can sign in to Steamworks.

steps.title: Pay the Steam Direct fee ($100)
steps.why: One fee per game; there is a 21-day wait after paying before you can release.
how: Steamworks > Pay the fee (Admin users only).
steps.tip: Pay early: the 30-day wait runs while you build the store page.

steps.title: Steam capsule images (exact sizes)
steps.why: Steam rejects images that are even one pixel off.
how: Rendered into release/06-steam/art: header 920x430, small 462x174, main 1232x706, vertical 748x896, library capsule 600x900, library header 920x430, library hero 3840x1240 (no text), library logo 1280x720 (transparent), page background 1438x810.
steps.tip: The small capsule must stay readable at 120 px wide: big logo, nothing else.
steps.done_when: All images exist at exact sizes.

steps.title: Store page: text, tags, screenshots, trailer
steps.why: Steam reviews the page before 'Coming soon' goes live.
how: Paste the Steam text from store-text.md; tags: Rhythm, Music, Casual, Family Friendly, Memory, Cute, Singleplayer.
Upload 5+ desktop screenshots and the trailer.
Content survey: no mature content.
steps.tip: Turn on 'Coming soon' as early as possible: every wishlist notifies a player on release day.

steps.title: Upload the build (SteamPipe)
steps.why: Steam installs from depots you upload.
how: Steamworks SDK > tools/ContentBuilder, or the web uploader for small builds. Depot layout notes in release/06-steam/README.md.
steps.tip: Set the launch option to the .exe and test with a Steam beta branch before release.
steps.done_when: The build installs and runs from your Steam library.

steps.title: Build review and release
steps.why: Valve checks the build before the release button unlocks.
how: Request build review; once approved and 30 days have passed since paying, press Release.
steps.tip: Release on a Tuesday-Thursday morning US time; avoid big sale weeks.

phases.name: GOG
phases.goal: Pitch the PC edition to GOG's curators.
phases.cost: Free to submit (GOG takes a revenue share if accepted)

steps.title: DRM-free, offline PC build
steps.why: GOG only sells games that run with no launcher or account.
how: The PC edition needs no internet, account or launcher; saves stay on the computer.
steps.tip: This is already true of the game's design.

steps.title: Write the GOG pitch
steps.why: GOG curates: a clear pitch matters as much as the game.
how: Draft in release/07-gog/pitch.md: what it is, who it's for, what's special (pure watch-and-copy, 40 levels, 4 maps, 100 skins, no ads, no tracking), links.
steps.tip: GOG favors polished single-player games; mention the family angle and that everything is earnable by playing.

steps.title: Submit to GOG
steps.why: GOG reviews every submission.
how: gog.com 'Submit your game' form: pitch, trailer, screenshots, a build or key.
steps.tip: Stronger after a Steam or itch.io launch with good reviews; GOG often asks about sales elsewhere.

steps.title: If accepted: contract and builds
steps.why: GOG sets up the store page and installers with you.
how: Sign the agreement, get Developer Portal access, upload Windows (and Mac/Linux) builds.
steps.tip: GOG Galaxy features (achievements) are optional.

phases.name: More stores (optional)
phases.goal: Extra reach once the main stores are live.
phases.cost: Microsoft free, Epic $100, Samsung and Amazon free

steps.title: Microsoft Store (Windows)
steps.why: Free for individual developers since 2025; the Store signs the app for you.
how: Sign up at storedeveloper.microsoft.com (ID check).
Package: PWABuilder.com from the beta link (fastest) or the Electron build as MSIX.
Age rating via IARC in Partner Center.
steps.tip: PWABuilder needs only the public beta link: no build machine required.

steps.title: Epic Games Store
steps.why: Another big PC store; 12% fee.
how: Epic Developer Portal, $100 per game, IARC rating, achievements set up, builds uploaded.
steps.tip: Epic requires achievements for new games; Claude can add a simple achievement set.

steps.title: Samsung Galaxy Store
steps.why: Preinstalled on Samsung phones; free to publish.
how: seller.samsungapps.com, upload the Android build, reuse the Play listing.
steps.tip: Samsung needs its own in-app purchase setup; launch it free-only at first if that's simpler.

steps.title: Amazon Appstore (Fire tablets)
steps.why: Fire tablets are popular with families.
how: developer.amazon.com, upload the Android build, reuse the Play listing.
steps.tip: Amazon Appstore now targets Fire devices only; test on a Fire tablet if you can.

phases.name: Launch and after
phases.goal: Launch smoothly, then keep players happy.

steps.title: Version 1.0.0 freeze and release notes
steps.why: Every store asks 'What's new'.
how: Claude writes release notes per store and tags the release in git.
steps.tip: Keep notes short and player-facing: new levels, fixes, nothing technical.

steps.title: Launch day
steps.why: The first week decides store rankings.
how: Post the store links to friends, family, social media and your testers.
Ask happy testers for an honest review in the first week.
steps.tip: Launch on one or two stores first, then add the others a week apart: each launch is a new reason to post.

steps.title: Weekly review of reviews and bug reports
steps.why: Quick fixes earn better ratings.
how: Once a week: you skim reviews; Claude reads the Bug & Feedback page and fixes what it can; one update per store.
steps.tip: Reply to every 1-3 star review with what you fixed.
steps.done_when: Ongoing: tick after your first weekly review.
